seoTitle: How to Make a Slideshow on Squarespace Easily
metaDescription: Build a photo slideshow on Squarespace by adding a Gallery section, choosing the slideshow layout, and configuring captions, animation, and lightbox.
intro: A slideshow is one of the fastest ways to give a Squarespace homepage or portfolio some visual weight without touching a line of code, but the option isn't labeled "slideshow" up front — it's a layout choice inside the Gallery section type, tucked in among grid and carousel alternatives. This guide walks through the real editor flow, starting from a published site, opening the Add a Section panel, and configuring the gallery's captions, animation, and lightbox settings so the finished slideshow actually fits the page.

steps.heading: Start from your site in edit mode
steps.body: Open your Squarespace site and enter the page editor for whichever page will hold the slideshow — in this example, a furniture and woodworking site called "PMN Online YT" with a hero section reading "Designed for Life" and navigation for About, Services, Gallery, and Book a Consultation. The top bar shows Save, Exit, and undo/redo controls, plus a Page label confirming you're editing the Home page and that it's currently Published — worth noting, since changes here go live once saved rather than sitting in a draft state.

image.caption: The Home page of a Squarespace site in edit mode, showing the published hero section before any gallery or slideshow has been added.

steps.heading: Open Add a Section and choose Images
steps.body: Click the add-content control where you want the slideshow to sit, which opens the Add a Section panel. Down the left side is a full list of section types — Testimonials, Events, Quotes, Digital Products, Scheduling, Donations, and further down, Images, Videos, Menus, Forms, and Charts. Selecting Images shows a live preview on the right with layout options, and a tooltip explains what these sections actually do: "These sections let you quickly add content items and switch between layouts without having to manually rearrange them." That's the key detail — the layout, including slideshow, is something you can change afterward without rebuilding the block.

image.caption: The Add a Section panel with Images selected, showing a gallery preview and a tooltip explaining that layouts can be switched without manually rearranging content.

steps.heading: Switch the layout to slideshow
steps.body: Once the gallery is added to the page, open its layout options — the same panel that let you choose Images in the first place also lets you switch between grid, carousel, and slideshow display styles for the same set of photos. Pick slideshow, and the block reflows to show one image at a time with navigation between them, rather than the grid of thumbnails you started with.

steps.heading: Configure captions, animation, and lightbox
steps.body: With the gallery selected, its settings panel opens with two tabs, Gallery and Colors. Under Gallery, a slider near the top controls image sizing, and below that sit the options that matter most for a slideshow: a Captions toggle to show or hide text under each image, an Animation dropdown defaulting to "Site Default" but changeable per-block, a Lightbox toggle that lets visitors click an image to view it enlarged, and a Divider toggle for adding a visual line under the section. There's also an Anchor Link field if you want to link directly to this slideshow from elsewhere on the page.

image.caption: The Gallery settings panel, with toggles for Captions, Lightbox, and Divider, plus an Animation dropdown and an anchor link field.

steps.heading: Add and reorder your images
steps.body: Add the photos you want in the rotation directly into the gallery block, and drag them into the order you want them to appear. Since the tooltip from the Add a Section step already confirmed this layout lets you rearrange content without rebuilding it, feel free to add more images than you need at first and trim or reorder later rather than getting the set perfect on the first pass.

steps.heading: Optimize images and preview on mobile
steps.body: Before publishing, compress your images so the slideshow loads quickly — large, uncompressed photos are the most common reason a slideshow feels sluggish on load. Use the device toggle near the top of the editor to preview how the slideshow looks on mobile, since captions and navigation controls that look fine on desktop can crowd a small screen, and it's easier to adjust settings now than after visitors start seeing it.

faq.question: Do I need a plugin to add a slideshow to Squarespace?
faq.answer: No — slideshow is a layout option built into the Images/Gallery section type, so no extra plugin or app is needed.

faq.question: Can I control how fast the slideshow moves?
faq.answer: Yes, the Animation setting in the Gallery panel controls transitions, and you can switch it from Site Default to a specific style per block.

faq.question: Will the slideshow look good on mobile?
faq.answer: Squarespace slideshows adapt to mobile automatically, but it's worth using the editor's device preview toggle to check captions and spacing on a small screen before publishing.

faq.question: How can I make my slideshow load faster?
faq.answer: Optimizing your images before uploading — reducing file size while keeping quality — helps the slideshow load quickly, especially since slideshow images often load ahead of the ones a visitor hasn't scrolled to yet.

faq.question: Can I switch between a grid, carousel, and slideshow later without starting over?
faq.answer: Yes — the layout options for an Images/Gallery section let you switch display styles for the same set of content without manually rearranging or re-adding your photos.
